Cc: dan.morris@promptsmith.ai, partners@promptsmith.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro — PromptSmith tracer + Redwood runtime proxy (commercial convo)

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for taking the quick intro last week. PromptSmith has completed a reference tracer implementation for LangChain and LlamaIndex and we'd like to explore a more formal commercial integration with Redwood Inference. Broad asks:

- Verify runtime compatibility with Redwood's continuous-batching and KV cache so our traces don't inflate latency.
- Define a distribution model (co-bundled SDK vs. hosted tracer endpoint + lightweight shim).
- Agree on support / escalation commitments for customers who consume both products.

Attached are our tracer spec and a one-page commercial term sheet — PTAL. The engineering dive would be small (2–3 engs, 2 weeks) if we go down the shim route.

[Attachment: promptsmith-tracer-specs.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]
[Attachment: promptsmith-commercial-term-sheet.xlsx (xlsx, 25KB)]

Can we get a short internal sync with Redwood eng/product to validate the integration and capture commercial options? I'm proposing Wed 16th or Thu 17th.

Thanks,
Hannah Lee
Head of Integrations | PromptSmith
https://promptsmith.ai

---

Note: PromptSmith is a third-party tooling vendor that provides distributed tracing for LLM runtimes (LangChain/LlamaIndex instrumentations, prompt-level tagging, experience dashboards).

Hannah — thanks for the materials, they're helpful. Quick notes from my side:

- This is definitely interesting for our ISV partner motion. Having a vetted tracer that understands hyperscaler batching and KV caching is useful for our platform customers.
- We prefer a shim/proxy approach that keeps the runtime binary minimal; co-bundling adds more release overhead for Dedicated/Private customers.
- We'd like to run a short compatibility spike: Redwood eng (Karthik) + PromptSmith eng (Dan) to smoke test with a small LangChain job and our dedicated runtime image.

Proposed next steps:
1) Short technical spike (2 weeks) to validate latency/overhead and instrumentation fidelity.
2) Draft SOW + term sheet for a joint distributed-tracing offering (commercial term sheet + support matrix).
3) If spike passes, pilot with one co-sell customer (we can propose a small PLG account).

Marissa, Karthik — can you join the technical sync if PromptSmith is available on Wed/Thu?

Looping in some quick commercial perspective — high level:

- We should clearly separate 1) technical validation (spike) and 2) commercialization steps. Keep the spike non-billable; we'll bill for integration work in the SOW.
- Consider a revenue share if PromptSmith drives incremental seats for Redwood Dedicated (20% suggested starting point).
- Ensure entitlements: private/on-prem customers require offline distribution licenses — we should include a checkbox in the term sheet.

Karthik — if the spike indicates <5% p50 token latency regression for typical sequences, I'm comfortable moving to an initial pilot. Anything above that and we need engineering mitigations (sampling, async emission).

Marissa Cole
Director, ISV Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Dan Morris <dan.morris@promptsmith.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro — PromptSmith tracer + Redwood runtime proxy (commercial convo)

Thanks all — Wed 16th 1pm PT works for our engs. Quick technical context before the spike:

- Our tracer has two modes: 1) in-process instrumentation (lighter weight hooks into LangChain/LlamaIndex SDKs) and 2) proxy emission where the runtime sends batched telemetry to a local shim that forwards to PromptSmith.
- For Redwood's runtime, mode (2) avoids touching the inference process and should reduce risk to latency. We'll prototype the proxy + small binary shim.

I attached a short developer guide and a minimal sampling config we use in production. We'll bring a small PoC branch to the sync.

[Attachment: promptsmith-devguide-tracer.pdf (pdf, 80KB)]

Looking forward — Dan
Dan Morris
CTO | PromptSmith
